classes/fighter/archetypes/dark-knight.h.title: Dark Knight
classes/fighter/archetypes/dark-knight.h.description:
Fighter⚔ Archetype.Stand stalwart in the face of danger, an immovable obstacle that your opponents must fight tooth and nail to merely walk past, let alone survive. Outside of combat your massive skill bonuses can allow you to sense what others don't, and sniff out liars.Based on the Maplestory class of the same name.
You can manifest an ominous looking eye that floats around you, enhancing your senses and giving you a palpable aura of menace. You get proficiency in +Intimidation😱 and +Insight🤔. You get a (4+½ LvL) bonus to +Perception👀, insight and intimidation. You also add this bonus to your will save against Demoralize.You can choose to make this eye disappear 1/turn as a free action, but you lose the bonuses to perception and intimidation.
All effects that grant elusive movement do not function against you while Evil Eye is active. Creatures can tell you still threaten to attack them in such cases.
If a creature tries to move around you using avoid AoO while wield a reach weapon, you add a bonus to your reflex save equal to the perception bonus granted by Evil Eye.
You get a +4 bonus to Fortitude saves. Your starting HP increases by 10. Each level after you gain an addition 4 hp.You take half damage from fortitude saves. When you pass a fort save, it deals no damage and has no additional effect.
You can make an infinite number of AoOs, and you have a +4 to Attack with AoOs.
When a creature ends its turn within your reach, it becomes shaken 1 (Will negates). Minions are automatically shaken.
You can leave behind a phantom weapon inside of your target on-hit. The creature is is unable to leave your natural reach and is Anchored. This condition only ends if you are disarmed, dazed, stunned, you or the target are moved out of reach or you are defeated.You can use this special attack an infinite number of times, but if you impale a second creature, the first is freed.
As a standard action, you can inspire all allies that can see you, giving them (10+4xLvL of creature) additional current and maximum hp until they rest, or until you are defeated.

classes/fighter/fighter.html.title: Fighter
classes/fighter/fighter.html.description:
Men-at-arms clad in steel that use various fighting styles to achieve the same goal: destroy as many enemies as possible using overwhelming martial prowess. Deadly Arsenal, Hearthstone
You have martial specialization.
You gain 1 technique point at level 1, then another point every 2 levels after. These technique points can be used on any martial tree.Once per any turn where you're capable of taking the attack action, you can make a simple attack as a free action, or as an additional simple attack if you do take the attack action.
You have +2 to Attack with weapons, natural attacks an unarmed strikes. You have DR 5 vs disarm.
Armors requires 2 less STR to use. You ignore the +Stealth penalty to heavy armor.
Gain athletics as a skill with a +4 bonus. You can Breakout an ally as a swift action, regardless of the action it usually took to breakout.
You have resistance to fear effects.When combat starts, if you are below full hp, heal to full HP.
When an enemy is a minion, you automatically know just by looking at them. Gain an additional superior attack that can only be used against minion enemies. You are immune to being grazed by minions
Gain Combat Reflexes as a bonus feat. If you already have it, gain a bonus feat. You can use an attack of opportunity to swat a ranged attack out of the air that targets either you or an ally within reach. Roll an attack roll. If your attack roll matches or exceeds theirs, the attack is negated.
You take a -4 attack penalty to attacks opposing siege weapons.
Your weapon attacks, natural attacks and unarmed attacks gain additional damage equal to their damage dice. Examples: 2h weapon @1=2d8, @6=4d8 Light Weapon @1=d6, @6=2d6
As a standard action you can enchant 2 different Weapons (including unarmed attacks and natural attacks) you hold with any quality from the magic weapon properties section, except Bane. You can enchant 2 different weapons, and give them different enchants. You can enchant new weapons, but the old ones lose their enchantments.Weapons cannot have typically more than 1 enchantment, unless they have multiple enchantment slots.

core-rules,-how-to-play/abbreviations-an.title: Concealment
core-rules,-how-to-play/abbreviations-an.description:
Concealment is a Circumstance that is gained when a creature's position is being obscured from another's Senses.
Usually, this means an effect like fog or darkness is partially or totally hiding a creature from another, resulting in Partial Concealment or Total Concealment, but this may take other forms against creatures that have other senses.
Concealment is a condition that's relative to the senses of other creatures. If you have Dark Vision and your opponent doesn't in a situation with Dark, you have concealment against them, but they don't have concealment to you.
Attacking from concealment, even Total Concealment, does not Surprise by default. You still need to use +Stealth as normal.
core-rules,-how-to-play/abbreviations-an.sourcePath: Core Rules, How to Play/Abbreviations and Terminology/Cover/Concealment.md

core-rules,-how-to-play/abbreviations-an.title: Cover
core-rules,-how-to-play/abbreviations-an.description:
Cover is an environmental Circumstance that increases your AC and Reflex by 2.
Standard Cover is received against Ranged Attacks and AoEs that target you while there are obstacles between you and the source of the attack that obscure a large portion of your space, and that cannot be pierced by the attack.
Better forms of cover result in Improved Cover and Total Cover.Examples include peeking around a pillar, over a trench, or behind a low wall.
core-rules,-how-to-play/abbreviations-an.sourcePath: Core Rules, How to Play/Abbreviations and Terminology/Cover/Cover.md

core-rules,-how-to-play/abbreviations-an.title: Improved Cover
core-rules,-how-to-play/abbreviations-an.description:
Improved Cover is an environmental Circumstance that increases your AC and Reflex by 4.
Improved Cover is received against Ranged Attacks and AoEs that target you while there are obstacles between you and the source of the attack that obscure almost all of your space, usually intentionally designed to allow attacks only in one direction, and that cannot be pierced by the attack.
Examples include arrow slits and murder holes., as well as ranged weapon attacks against Submerged targets.
core-rules,-how-to-play/abbreviations-an.sourcePath: Core Rules, How to Play/Abbreviations and Terminology/Cover/Improved Cover.md

core-rules,-how-to-play/abbreviations-an.title: Partial Concealment
core-rules,-how-to-play/abbreviations-an.description: Partial Concealment is a Circumstance that decreases attacker's ACC by 2. When you have Partial Concealment, a creature can still see you, but in a limited capacity. Either they can only see your shadow, they're trying to avert your gaze, or there are poor environmental conditions/magic at play.
core-rules,-how-to-play/abbreviations-an.sourcePath: Core Rules, How to Play/Abbreviations and Terminology/Cover/Partial Concealment.md

core-rules,-how-to-play/abbreviations-an.title: Total Concealment
core-rules,-how-to-play/abbreviations-an.description:
Total Concealment is a Circumstance that decreases attacker's ACC by 4.
When you have Total Concealment, a creature cannot see you at all. Either they are Blinded, you are completely hidden in an environmental or magical effect, or you are Invisible.
core-rules,-how-to-play/abbreviations-an.sourcePath: Core Rules, How to Play/Abbreviations and Terminology/Cover/Total Concealment.md

core-rules,-how-to-play/abbreviations-an.title: Total Cover
core-rules,-how-to-play/abbreviations-an.description:
Total Cover is an environmental Circumstance that makes you Untargetable.
Total Cover is received against Ranged Attacks, AoEs, and Core Rules, How to Play/Attacking/Target Abilities that target you while there are obstacles between you and the source of the attack that leave no way to reach you, and that cannot be pierced by the attack (in the case of Ranged Attacks and Area Effects.)
core-rules,-how-to-play/abbreviations-an.sourcePath: Core Rules, How to Play/Abbreviations and Terminology/Cover/Total Cover.md

core-rules,-how-to-play/abbreviations-an.title: Abbreviations
core-rules,-how-to-play/abbreviations-an.description:
AC - Armor Class
Attack - Accuracy
AoE - Area of Effect
CC - Debilitating Status AKA Crowd Control
GM - Dungeon Master
+HP - Hit Points
LvL - Level
NPC - Non-Player Character
PC - Player Character
CHA - Charisma
DEX - Dexterity
INT - Intelligence
LUK - Luck
STR - Strength
WIS - Wisdom
AoO - Attack of Opportunity
Crit - Critical Hit
DC - Difficulty Class AKA Target Number
Dismissible - Dismissible
core-rules,-how-to-play/abbreviations-an.sourcePath: Core Rules, How to Play/Abbreviations and Terminology/Abbreviations.md

core-rules,-how-to-play/abbreviations-an.title: AC
core-rules,-how-to-play/abbreviations-an.description:
Armor Class (AC) is the measure of how difficult it is to hit you. Targets must meet or exceed your AC with an Attack Roll to Damage you.
By default, your starting AC is 10, and you add your LvL and Armor. DEX also gets added, but see Armor for how dex interacts with armor. It is also adjusted based on Circumstance.
core-rules,-how-to-play/abbreviations-an.sourcePath: Core Rules, How to Play/Abbreviations and Terminology/AC.md

core-rules,-how-to-play/abbreviations-an.title: AoE
core-rules,-how-to-play/abbreviations-an.description: Stands for "Area of Effect." It is used as shorthand to describe an attack that affects a wide area, such as an explosion, or a line of fire from a dragon's breath.Area attacks have a point of origin. When the origin is a creature, such as with a breath weapon, determine Cover from one specific point in its occupied space. If the origin is a targeted point in space, such as with an explosion radiating outward, that point should be used to determine cover.
core-rules,-how-to-play/abbreviations-an.sourcePath: Core Rules, How to Play/Abbreviations and Terminology/AoE.md

core-rules,-how-to-play/abbreviations-an.title: CC
core-rules,-how-to-play/abbreviations-an.description: A Debilitating Status (CC) is one that impedes your movement or prevents you from taking actions normally.
core-rules,-how-to-play/abbreviations-an.sourcePath: Core Rules, How to Play/Abbreviations and Terminology/CC.md

core-rules,-how-to-play/abbreviations-an.title: Circumstance
core-rules,-how-to-play/abbreviations-an.description:
Circumstance is any in-game situation, event, or position that conditionally applies a bonus, penalty, or Status to a creature.
Circumstances can apply to different creatures in different ways, usually based on positioning or the presence or absence of abilities - for example, having a low wall to grant you Cover will work for any creatures on the other side of the wall, but not on the same side as you. One creature may see you while you're in a cloud, while another cannot. You may be above one creature, but another creature may be above you. Therefore, these effects are circumstantial.
core-rules,-how-to-play/abbreviations-an.sourcePath: Core Rules, How to Play/Abbreviations and Terminology/Circumstance.md

core-rules,-how-to-play/abbreviations-an.title: DC
core-rules,-how-to-play/abbreviations-an.description: Difficulty Class (DC) is the target number that a Roll must reach to be considered a success.
core-rules,-how-to-play/abbreviations-an.sourcePath: Core Rules, How to Play/Abbreviations and Terminology/DC.md

core-rules,-how-to-play/abbreviations-an.title: DR
core-rules,-how-to-play/abbreviations-an.description:
Damage Reduction (DR) is a rare form of defense that reduces incoming damage by a flat amount, noted as a value (DR x). DR applies to slash, pierce, crush and Poise damage, and DRA applies to all Damage types (minus True Damage). All DR stacks.
Stacking defenses works in the way that protects the most - such as applying DR after Resistance. If an effect's damage is reduced to 0 with DR, then any associated non-damaging effects are negated.DR cannot block damage from the same attack twice, such as from a flaming sword, or an attack that deals poise damage and hp damage.
core-rules,-how-to-play/abbreviations-an.sourcePath: Core Rules, How to Play/Abbreviations and Terminology/DR.md

core-rules,-how-to-play/abbreviations-an.title: Flanking
core-rules,-how-to-play/abbreviations-an.description: Flanking is a Circumstance that grants +2 Attack against a target that you and an ally are Threatening from opposite sides.
core-rules,-how-to-play/abbreviations-an.sourcePath: Core Rules, How to Play/Abbreviations and Terminology/Flanking.md

core-rules,-how-to-play/abbreviations-an.title: Initiative
core-rules,-how-to-play/abbreviations-an.description:
Nick Nacks is a turn-based game, and initiative decides who goes firstOne of the players rolls a d10. On a 6 or higher, the players go first, or a 5 or lower, the enemies go first. On the first round of combat, whichever party went first decides which creature acts first. Then you swap to the other party and they decide who goes. You repeat this process until either every creature has acted, or one side has several creatures that haven't acted. All remaining creatures act on the same turn and then you start back from the top, using the same order as round 1.When initiative is rolled, all Buff effects disappear automatically (unless its duration is longer than 1 minute). This is to discourage spamming buffing spells and then waiting to recover mana.
Surprise In DnD and its derivatives, if you get the jump on your opponent, the sneaky party gets an entire turn to themselves. This is not the case in Nick Nacks. The conventional "surprise round" is now a normal round in combat.All characters that are surprised lose are DD during the first round, and the surprising party always goes first in initiative. Surprise can be a bit finicky sometimes, making you question if only some characters should be surprised. If that's what your gut tells you, that's how it is.For example, your party's rogue who was hiding in an alley ambushes a group of guardsmen that are harassing the rest of the party. The guard captain notices but his men do not. Captain is not DD, the rest are.What happens when our party starts fighting in the middle of talking? In the event where there are two parties that don't immediately fight, when initiative starts is usually determined by whenever someone takes an aggressive action, such as casting a spell or drawing an arrow. In these cases, where both parties are aware of each other, initiative gets rolled immediately before any actions happen.Certain types of underhanded tactics can get around this, such as using sleight of hand to draw concealed weapons or deception for a sucker punch. See surprise for more details.
core-rules,-how-to-play/abbreviations-an.sourcePath: Core Rules, How to Play/Abbreviations and Terminology/Initiative.md

core-rules,-how-to-play/abbreviations-an.title: Minion
core-rules,-how-to-play/abbreviations-an.description: Minion is a Circumstantial label assigned to a creature as it relates to another. A creature that is 1/3 of the level of another or lower is a Minion compared to it.A level 0 creature is always considered a Minion to any creature of a higher level.
core-rules,-how-to-play/abbreviations-an.sourcePath: Core Rules, How to Play/Abbreviations and Terminology/Minion.md

core-rules,-how-to-play/abbreviations-an.title: Natural
core-rules,-how-to-play/abbreviations-an.description: A Natural result on a Roll is the result without any bonuses or penalties.
core-rules,-how-to-play/abbreviations-an.sourcePath: Core Rules, How to Play/Abbreviations and Terminology/Natural.md

core-rules,-how-to-play/abbreviations-an.title: NPC
core-rules,-how-to-play/abbreviations-an.description:
Non-Player Character (NPC): Any character that is played by the GM.
These characters usually get placed after PCs to favor the players.
core-rules,-how-to-play/abbreviations-an.sourcePath: Core Rules, How to Play/Abbreviations and Terminology/NPC.md

core-rules,-how-to-play/abbreviations-an.title: PC
core-rules,-how-to-play/abbreviations-an.description: Player Character (PC): A character controlled by a player, and not the GM. Players are the main characters of a story, and thus gain priority in some aspects.Sometimes, a DM will play a special character alongside the players that is treated like a PC. This is normal, but the players can veto such a character's PC status if they feel it is inappropriate.
core-rules,-how-to-play/abbreviations-an.sourcePath: Core Rules, How to Play/Abbreviations and Terminology/PC.md

core-rules,-how-to-play/abbreviations-an.title: Roll
core-rules,-how-to-play/abbreviations-an.description: The default die roll for resolving things. This is used to determine the variance expected.In Nick Nacks, this is a 20 sided dice for most rolls. Other dice are typically only used in damage rolls and other niche cases.
core-rules,-how-to-play/abbreviations-an.sourcePath: Core Rules, How to Play/Abbreviations and Terminology/Roll.md

core-rules,-how-to-play/abbreviations-an.title: Sp
core-rules,-how-to-play/abbreviations-an.description: Spell abilities encompass any ability that is magical that is a Spell.Sometimes used in notation for abilities that mimic or function like spells.
core-rules,-how-to-play/abbreviations-an.sourcePath: Core Rules, How to Play/Abbreviations and Terminology/Sp.md

core-rules,-how-to-play/abbreviations-an.title: Su
core-rules,-how-to-play/abbreviations-an.description:
Supernatural abilities encompass any ability that is magical, but not a Spell.
Many supernatural abilities are persistent effects on a creature. If such a thing is ever dispelled, then if must be reactivated as a swift action.
core-rules,-how-to-play/abbreviations-an.sourcePath: Core Rules, How to Play/Abbreviations and Terminology/Su.md

core-rules,-how-to-play/abbreviations-an.title: Threaten
core-rules,-how-to-play/abbreviations-an.description: The area a creature threatens represents where they can make attacks. This usually only applies to melee attacks. This area also marks where it is typically not safe to perform certain actions, or risk getting hit with an AoO.
core-rules,-how-to-play/abbreviations-an.sourcePath: Core Rules, How to Play/Abbreviations and Terminology/Threaten.md

core-rules,-how-to-play/abbreviations-an.title: XP
core-rules,-how-to-play/abbreviations-an.description:
Crusty content Experience is a meta-currency gained through prioritizing primary campaign events that allows players to influence the story/chronological order of things in order to accomplish personal goals quickly and get back into the action faster. As a baseline, 10 XP is the equivalent of one in-game day of events.
Experience is rewarded for spending time working towards campaign goals in an active manner. This mainly means exploring dungeons, splitting heads, and overthrowing governments - anything that is both related to the main campaign objectives, and is not part of downtime events (such as recovering from an Affliction or Crafting). XP is rewarded based on the time required to complete the mission, with additional bonuses for overcoming particular challenges. The purpose of XP is to reward taking action. While downtime is an important part of roleplay, it's easy to justify staying in town making safe money or doing side quests to save up for a shiny new weapon or achieve personal goals if there isn't an obvious time constraint on important story events. It's easy to hold off on an important event and try to squeeze a few more days of crafting into your schedule. Instead, XP serves to reward taking action immediately, without penalizing downtime events like crafting.
core-rules,-how-to-play/abbreviations-an.sourcePath: Core Rules, How to Play/Abbreviations and Terminology/XP.md

core-rules,-how-to-play/ability-scores/a.title: Ability Scores
core-rules,-how-to-play/ability-scores/a.description:
These are representations of a creature's innate or cultivated affinities. These represent the mind, body, and spirit. The ability scores are Strength, Dexterity, Luck, Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma.
Every Player Character gets 6 points to increase their ability scores as they wish, starting from 0 in each.You can decrease a ability scores to -1 in order to gain an additional point. The maximum points you can invest in a given ability score is 3.
core-rules,-how-to-play/ability-scores/a.sourcePath: Core Rules, How to Play/Ability Scores/Ability Scores.md

core-rules,-how-to-play/ability-scores/c.title: Carry Weight
core-rules,-how-to-play/ability-scores/c.description: A creature's Carry Weight represents what it is capable of lifting and moving around with without much effort.The default value is 100.A creature can lift and drag twice as much as their carry weight, but is staggered while doing so.
core-rules,-how-to-play/ability-scores/c.sourcePath: Core Rules, How to Play/Ability Scores/Carry Weight.md

core-rules,-how-to-play/ability-scores/c.title: CHA
core-rules,-how-to-play/ability-scores/c.description:
Your leadership and personal magnetism. Positive charisma enhances your Companion creatures. Any creature that takes a companion slot gains your CHA to their Accuracy
With positive charisma, you get a teamwork feat For every point of CHA, you can grant another creature one of your teamwork feats. To do this, you must spend 1 hour doing training exercises with the creatures you intend to team up with You lose a companion slot with negative CHA. Negative CHA reduces your companion's Accuracy You cannot benefit from teamwork feats with negative charisma
core-rules,-how-to-play/ability-scores/c.sourcePath: Core Rules, How to Play/Ability Scores/CHA.md

core-rules,-how-to-play/ability-scores/d.title: DEX
core-rules,-how-to-play/ability-scores/d.description:
Your agility, hand-eye coordination, and general sneakiness. You add DEX to your Reflex Save.
Depending on your choice in armor, you can add your dexterity to your AC, but you always add it to Poise
You add dexterity to Attack and Damage with ranged weapons and light weapons (but not at the same time as strength)
Every point of DEX adds +5 to your Land Speed Negative DEX subtracts from these values.
core-rules,-how-to-play/ability-scores/d.sourcePath: Core Rules, How to Play/Ability Scores/DEX.md

core-rules,-how-to-play/ability-scores/i.title: INT
core-rules,-how-to-play/ability-scores/i.description:
Your knowledge, magical expertise, and logic capacity. You gain an additional point of Memory per point of INT
You gain an additional Skill Proficiency per point of INT
You gain two additional Languages per point of INT
You gain a Mana reserve for each point in intelligence Negative int subtracts from these values. In particular, you lose max mana equal to your negative int. Intelligence and Sentience A creature is considered sentient if it has at least -2 intelligence. These creatures typically do not speak, but can understand at least 1 language.Animal intelligence is -3 intelligence. Creatures with animal intelligence only understand simple commands (if anything). They are usually limited to their instinctual urges.Mindless creatures possess no will of their own. They act completely on instinct.
core-rules,-how-to-play/ability-scores/i.sourcePath: Core Rules, How to Play/Ability Scores/INT.md

core-rules,-how-to-play/ability-scores/l.title: Luck Check
core-rules,-how-to-play/ability-scores/l.description: Luck checks are dice rolls that only add the creatures LUK stat. Separate from Serendipity checks, which are a more specific type of luck check.
core-rules,-how-to-play/ability-scores/l.sourcePath: Core Rules, How to Play/Ability Scores/Luck Check.md

core-rules,-how-to-play/ability-scores/l.title: LUK
core-rules,-how-to-play/ability-scores/l.description:
Your ability to turn tides and benefit from unlikely outcomes. You get a number of Boons🍀 equal to your LUK score
You add LUK to Luck Checks.
You can add LUK to a Roll as an Immediate Action (that did not already add LUK). You must roll to add luck, so you cannot add it when you take 10 (such as when using skills for income) or take 20 Negative LUK give you a bane per point of negative luck
Your DC decreases by your negative luck Subtracted from luck checks
core-rules,-how-to-play/ability-scores/l.sourcePath: Core Rules, How to Play/Ability Scores/LUK.md

core-rules,-how-to-play/ability-scores/s.title: STR
core-rules,-how-to-play/ability-scores/s.description:
Your fortitude, athleticism, and endurance. You add STR to your Fortitude Save.
You add STR to your Poise
You add +100 Carry Weight for each point of strength
Every point of strength increases your Enhanced Jump distance by 5 ft. Negative STR subtracts from your Fortitude Saves. Negative STR halves your Carry Weight.
core-rules,-how-to-play/ability-scores/s.sourcePath: Core Rules, How to Play/Ability Scores/STR.md

core-rules,-how-to-play/ability-scores/w.title: WIS
core-rules,-how-to-play/ability-scores/w.description:
Your faith, decision making, habits, diligence, and discipline. You add WIS to your Will Save.
You add your wisdom to +Perception👀, the skill all creatures get for free
You can pray to your god for guidance (see below for details). You can use prayer a number of times per day equal to your wisdom bonus. You can also use it for Invoking Deities.
Positive wisdom increases GBP gains, giving you deific boons boons earlier and in higher quantities Negative WIS subtracts from these values Negative wisdom represents a complete lack of faith in most gods or being rejected by them, you cannot gain GBP (unless in service of Frogg Saran)
core-rules,-how-to-play/ability-scores/w.sourcePath: Core Rules, How to Play/Ability Scores/WIS.md

core-rules,-how-to-play/actions/action-s.title: Burrow
core-rules,-how-to-play/actions/action-s.description:
Burrow Speeds allow Movement through dirt, clay, and other particulate turf, but not solid rocks (unless otherwise stated). Burrowing leaves a temporary hole the size of the creature that burrowed for a few rounds, depending on the sediment type, unless the creature takes measures to avoid this.
Starting to burrow is a Swift Action that Provokes as if leaving a Threatened space.
core-rules,-how-to-play/actions/action-s.sourcePath: Core Rules, How to Play/Actions/Action System/Movement/Burrow.md

core-rules,-how-to-play/actions/action-s.title: Difficult Terrain
core-rules,-how-to-play/actions/action-s.description: Difficult Terrain is a Circumstance that represents reduced movement due to physical blockage. This can be because of wading through knee-deep mud, flying through dense brush, or burrowing through particularly rocky turf.
core-rules,-how-to-play/actions/action-s.sourcePath: Core Rules, How to Play/Actions/Action System/Movement/Difficult Terrain.md

core-rules,-how-to-play/actions/action-s.title: Fly
core-rules,-how-to-play/actions/action-s.description:
Fly Speeds allow Movement in any direction, treating spaces moving directly into the air as Difficult Terrain.
A creature that is Entangled or Grounded cannot continue flight.
A creature that takes +HP damage from an Attack Roll or AoE effect while flying receives Clumsy 1 until they land, at which point the clumsy is removed.
Starting to fly is a Swift Action that Provokes as if leaving a Threatened space. Some mobility effects that place you into the air like Sky Uppercut or Extreme Speed can reasonably bypass this action requirement.
core-rules,-how-to-play/actions/action-s.sourcePath: Core Rules, How to Play/Actions/Action System/Movement/Fly.md

core-rules,-how-to-play/actions/action-s.title: Hover
core-rules,-how-to-play/actions/action-s.description:
Hover is a lesser version of [[flight, where the creature is limited to hovering a few feet above the ground. Hover Speeds allow Movement above solid and liquid surfaces while ignoring Difficult Terrain.
A creature that is Grounded cannot hover.
core-rules,-how-to-play/actions/action-s.sourcePath: Core Rules, How to Play/Actions/Action System/Movement/Hover.md

core-rules,-how-to-play/actions/action-s.title: Movement
core-rules,-how-to-play/actions/action-s.description: You can move up to your Land Speed on your turn. Some abilities or effects may require spending a certain amount of your movement for the turn. Abilities that move you do not cost or consume any of your movement unless otherwise stated.
core-rules,-how-to-play/actions/action-s.sourcePath: Core Rules, How to Play/Actions/Action System/Movement/Movement.md

core-rules,-how-to-play/actions/action-s.title: Action System
core-rules,-how-to-play/actions/action-s.description:
This game is played turn-based, with turn order determined at the start of the battle with an Initiative roll. The actions you can take on your turn are as follows. Standard Action: This action occupies most of your turn, and you can perform one per turn.
Swift Action: This action can be executed during any other action, with a limit of one per turn.
Free Action: These actions are effortless or part of other actions, allowing you to perform as many as you wish per turn - within reason.
Full-Round Action: This action requires the use of your standard action and all of your Movement. You may still move if you have an ability that allows extra movement as a different action.
Movement: You can move up to your Speed on your turn. Some abilities or effects may require spending a certain amount of your movement for the turn. You may have other forms of movement that manifest in terms of different Speeds - you may use multiple forms of movement on the same turn, but only up to the maximum amount for the given speed. Any slower speeds used overlap - That is, if you have a Fly 40 and a ground speed of 30, you may walk 30 feet and then fly another 10. When it's not your turn, you can take the following actions:
Immediate Action: A Swift Action that can occur off-turn. Limited to one per round, shared with Swift Action — you cannot use both in the same round.
Instant Action: A Free Action that can occur off-turn. Referred to as "Instantly" in abilities.
Attack of Opportunity: A response triggered by certain actions of others. Limited to one per round. When a creature "Provokes," they are engaging in an action that allows others to AoO them.
core-rules,-how-to-play/actions/action-s.sourcePath: Core Rules, How to Play/Actions/Action System/Action System.md

core-rules,-how-to-play/actions/action-s.title: AoO
core-rules,-how-to-play/actions/action-s.description: Short for "Attack of Opportunity"An AoO is an Instant Action Attack Roll triggered in response to certain actions of others. All creatures can do this once per round by default. When a creature "Provokes," they are engaging in an action that allows others to AoO them.An AoO always happens before the triggering action.Movement can only provoke once from a given creature per turn.
core-rules,-how-to-play/actions/action-s.sourcePath: Core Rules, How to Play/Actions/Action System/AoO.md

core-rules,-how-to-play/actions/action-s.title: Free Action
core-rules,-how-to-play/actions/action-s.description:
Free Action: These actions are effortless or part of other actions, allowing you to perform as many as you wish per turn - within reason. See: Delay
Swap Item
+Monster Lore📖
core-rules,-how-to-play/actions/action-s.sourcePath: Core Rules, How to Play/Actions/Action System/Free Action.md

core-rules,-how-to-play/actions/action-s.title: Full-Round Action
core-rules,-how-to-play/actions/action-s.description: Full-Round Action: This action requires the use of your standard action and all of your movement. You may still move if you have an ability that allows extra movement as a different action.
core-rules,-how-to-play/actions/action-s.sourcePath: Core Rules, How to Play/Actions/Action System/Full-Round Action.md

core-rules,-how-to-play/actions/action-s.title: Immediate Action
core-rules,-how-to-play/actions/action-s.description: A Swift Action that can occur off-turn. Limited to one per round, shared with Swift Action — you cannot use both in the same round.You cannot use an immediate action AND an instant action in response to the same trigger, ie taking the Block action for you and an ally against a Kazekenshin Steel Tempest.
core-rules,-how-to-play/actions/action-s.sourcePath: Core Rules, How to Play/Actions/Action System/Immediate Action.md

core-rules,-how-to-play/actions/action-s.title: Instant Action
core-rules,-how-to-play/actions/action-s.description: A Free Action that can occur off-turn.You cannot use an immediate action AND an instant action, or multiple instant actions, in response to the same trigger, ie taking the Block action for you and an ally against a Kazekenshin Steel Tempest.
core-rules,-how-to-play/actions/action-s.sourcePath: Core Rules, How to Play/Actions/Action System/Instant Action.md

core-rules,-how-to-play/actions/action-s.title: Standard Action
core-rules,-how-to-play/actions/action-s.description:
Standard Action: This action occupies most of your turn, and you can perform one per turn. You can also use your standard action to perform a swift action. Example: The Attack Action is the most common, allowing a series of smaller attacks up to your Attack Speed, executed in any order. Refer to the "Attack" section for more details. See: Administer Potion
Aid
Carry
Charge
Dash
Disengage
Prepare
Total Defense
core-rules,-how-to-play/actions/action-s.sourcePath: Core Rules, How to Play/Actions/Action System/Standard Action.md

core-rules,-how-to-play/actions/action-s.title: Swift Action
core-rules,-how-to-play/actions/action-s.description:
Swift Action: This action can be executed during any other action, with a limit of one per turn. See: Hide
Enhanced Jump
Use Potion
Recharge Abilities
core-rules,-how-to-play/actions/action-s.sourcePath: Core Rules, How to Play/Actions/Action System/Swift Action.md

core-rules,-how-to-play/actions/common-a.title: Delay
core-rules,-how-to-play/actions/common-a.description: You can decide to wait to act in initiative, acting whenever you like at the end of another creature's turn, permanently changing your position in initiative.
core-rules,-how-to-play/actions/common-a.sourcePath: Core Rules, How to Play/Actions/Common Actions/Free Actions/Delay.md

core-rules,-how-to-play/actions/common-a.title: Swap Item
core-rules,-how-to-play/actions/common-a.description: At the start of your turn, you can decide what's in your hands from your inventory. You can draw and put away any weapons without penalty. This is a free action as long as it's done at the start of your turn. If you decide to change what you're wielding at another point in your turn, it becomes a swift action - and you can't do both.
core-rules,-how-to-play/actions/common-a.sourcePath: Core Rules, How to Play/Actions/Common Actions/Free Actions/Swap Item.md

core-rules,-how-to-play/actions/common-a.title: Administer Potion
core-rules,-how-to-play/actions/common-a.description: Give a potion to an unconscious ally. You can use potions from either of your inventories.A conscious ally must spend an Immediate Action to drink an administered potion.
core-rules,-how-to-play/actions/common-a.sourcePath: Core Rules, How to Play/Actions/Common Actions/Standard Actions/Administer Potion.md

core-rules,-how-to-play/actions/common-a.title: Aid
core-rules,-how-to-play/actions/common-a.description:
Provide one of the following bonuses to an ally within your reach for 1 round:+2 to Attack
+2 to Saves
+2 to AC
Alternatively, remove one stack of the following conditions: Clumsy, Shaken, Sickened. It can also remove the charmed or Knocked Down conditions. You can also use aid to breakout any ally trapped by objects.You can aid a defeated creature when not in combat, bringing them to 1 hp. Extreme circumstances may require more assistance to restore a creature particularly out of it (such as medicine or magic).
core-rules,-how-to-play/actions/common-a.sourcePath: Core Rules, How to Play/Actions/Common Actions/Standard Actions/Aid.md

core-rules,-how-to-play/actions/common-a.title: Carry
core-rules,-how-to-play/actions/common-a.description: Carrying an ally allows you to move them with your movement. You must be able to lift the ally. If you can't, you drag them, treating all terrain as difficult terrain. You must use this action every turn you carry an ally. The creature you carry becomes clumsy 2 unless they are defeated or you aren't in combat.
core-rules,-how-to-play/actions/common-a.sourcePath: Core Rules, How to Play/Actions/Common Actions/Standard Actions/Carry.md

core-rules,-how-to-play/actions/common-a.title: Dash
core-rules,-how-to-play/actions/common-a.description: Double your speed this round. Has no effect if your speed is zero.
core-rules,-how-to-play/actions/common-a.sourcePath: Core Rules, How to Play/Actions/Common Actions/Standard Actions/Dash.md

core-rules,-how-to-play/actions/common-a.title: Disengage
core-rules,-how-to-play/actions/common-a.description: Your movement is Elusive this turn.
core-rules,-how-to-play/actions/common-a.sourcePath: Core Rules, How to Play/Actions/Common Actions/Standard Actions/Disengage.md

core-rules,-how-to-play/actions/common-a.title: Prepare
core-rules,-how-to-play/actions/common-a.description: You can prepare swift actions, movement, free actions and standard actions to react to a specific triggering event (Ex: “a goblin opens this door, I walk up to him and shove him off the cliff”). If the triggering action never happens, you don't get your actions back.When you prepare a standard action to attack, you can only prepare a single attack.You cannot prepare actions outside of Initiative.
core-rules,-how-to-play/actions/common-a.sourcePath: Core Rules, How to Play/Actions/Common Actions/Standard Actions/Prepare.md

core-rules,-how-to-play/actions/common-a.title: Total Defense
core-rules,-how-to-play/actions/common-a.description: Get DRA 2 until the start of your next turn. Remove all clumsy stacks and reset your poise to maximum. You can't make an AoO while using Total Defense.
core-rules,-how-to-play/actions/common-a.sourcePath: Core Rules, How to Play/Actions/Common Actions/Standard Actions/Total Defense.md

core-rules,-how-to-play/alternative-win-.title: Alternative Win Conditions
core-rules,-how-to-play/alternative-win-.description: For when killing everything that moves isn't what you want, alternative win conditions seek to answer the question of "How do I end combat without reducing the enemy hp to 0?"
core-rules,-how-to-play/alternative-win-.sourcePath: Core Rules, How to Play/Alternative Win Conditions/Alternative Win Conditions.md

core-rules,-how-to-play/alternative-win-.title: Restraint
core-rules,-how-to-play/alternative-win-.description: When creatures don't surrender, but you don’t want to risk killing them, restraints can be used to end the fight. Some situations can naturally be neutralized by dropping a cage in the right place, but such conveniences are rare. More often than not, restraining your foe is going to involves rope and cuffs.Grabbing and already-grabbed creature allows you to put cuffs on them.One grab is needed per appendage cuffed. You cannot cuff a creature on your own unless you can grab multiple times per turn, in which case you need another free hand. This provokes AoO.This completely prevents the use of their arms outside of simple item interactions. Cuffs can also be placed on the legs to reduce a creatures speed to 15. Combat maneuvers made against a cuffed creature gain a +10 bonus.Cuffs are difficult to escape, and even harder to break. They typically require outside assistance in order to be removed. Because cuffs are typically made from iron and steel, they can take a significant beating.DC to break (Athletics) or lockpick (Hands) is dependent on the type of material and the lock. A typical forged cuff is DC 40 to break, or 20 to pick.Creatures that are bound can try to free themselves, but take a -5 penalty.Grabbing and already-grabbed creature allows you to tie them with rope.One grab is needed per appendage tied. You cannot tie up a creature on your own unless you can grab multiple times per turn, in which case you need another free hand. This provokes AoO.Rope is easier to destroy than cuffs, but it is also easier to make the restraint more intense. By grabbing one more time, you can prevent the creature from acting completely.Rope tends to be a good way to bind singular creatures, since anybody with a sharp implement can handily free a bound creature.Rope can be destroyed with an attack from any slashing weapon. Using Athletics or Acrobatics, you can pull the ropes apart, but the DC is determined by the athletics bonus of the creature who bound you (30+their athletics bonus). Creatures that are bound can try to free themselves, but take a -5 penalty. This penalty can be ignored with a natural attack suitable for freeing yourself, or a slashing concealed weapon.Grabbing and already-grabbed creature allows you to forcefully shove them into an object within reach such as a bag, barrel, or box, so long as they can handily fit in the object.Whether or not they can escape generally depends on the object and the tools the captured creature has on hand. Wooden crates don’t do to well when trying to hold barbarians or crafty characters with crowbars.DC to break (Athletics) is dependent on the type of material. Some objects can be handily dealt with, not requiring a skill check. A knife makes quick work of a bag, and given enough space, hammers break boxes.Creatures that are bound can try to free themselves, but take a -5 penalty.
core-rules,-how-to-play/alternative-win-.sourcePath: Core Rules, How to Play/Alternative Win Conditions/Restraint.md

core-rules,-how-to-play/alternative-win-.title: Surrender and Morale
core-rules,-how-to-play/alternative-win-.description:
During combat there come times when you do not wish to fight, usually when one side is close to victory, but can also happen when creatures are clearly outnumbered or outmatched.How well a surrender feels in a situation usually comes down to a gut feeling, affected by a lot of variables. In order to even consider a surrender to be viable, one or more of the following (or other applicable) conditions should be met…
Numbers advantage
Some other clear advantage, such as terrain, positioning, equipment or a powerful noteworthy ally
Heavily damaged or unconscious allies
Consequences for not surrendering (often death or further prosecution)
Hostages
Whether or not creatures are minions or named characters
A surrender requires clear communication, which may not always be possible given the hectic and spread out nature of battle. Some creatures, particularly mindless ones, will not surrender unless specific circumstances are met. Creatures of animal intelligence can be convinced to surrender if you can speak to animals or have wild empathy etc.Surrender can mean forfeiting weapons, fleeing in fear, begging for mercy or something similar. If not all individuals accept the surrender, then the fight continues until they do.
core-rules,-how-to-play/alternative-win-.sourcePath: Core Rules, How to Play/Alternative Win Conditions/Surrender and Morale.md

core-rules,-how-to-play/alternative-win-.title: Truce
core-rules,-how-to-play/alternative-win-.description: In situations where there are two opposing sides that are generally neutral towards each other or even allies with each other, you can call for a truce. This generally requires important information (we were sent by the merchants guild), certification from an important or recognizable organization (legal documentation) or a special item (an artifact or flag).It could also be appropriate to call for a truce if you are delving into a dungeon and encounter another party, so long as you aren't after the same thing. You might not cooperate, but at least you won't be killing each other. If more information is revealed by talking throughout a battle (wait you're also hunting for the garbooni?), you can also reasonably call for a truce.
core-rules,-how-to-play/alternative-win-.sourcePath: Core Rules, How to Play/Alternative Win Conditions/Truce.md

core-rules,-how-to-play/attacking/combat.title: Dirty Trick
core-rules,-how-to-play/attacking/combat.description: Apply clumsy 1, sickened 1 or blurred vision to a creature. They must spend a standard action to get rid of the condition.
core-rules,-how-to-play/attacking/combat.sourcePath: Core Rules, How to Play/Attacking/Combat Maneuvers/Dirty Trick.md

core-rules,-how-to-play/attacking/combat.title: Disarm
core-rules,-how-to-play/attacking/combat.description: Knock a held item out of a creature’s hand, landing at their feet. It takes 30 ft of Movement or a Standard Action to pick up an item off the ground, which Provokes.
core-rules,-how-to-play/attacking/combat.sourcePath: Core Rules, How to Play/Attacking/Combat Maneuvers/Disarm.md

core-rules,-how-to-play/attacking/combat.title: Drag
core-rules,-how-to-play/attacking/combat.description: Requires a free hand or prehensile appendage. Target creature stays adjacent to you for the remainder of your turn, up to 30 ft. This is reduced to 10 feet if they are larger than you and you do not possess exceptional strength with which to carry them. If the creature is not adjacent to you when you successfully drag, they are automatically pulled adjacent to you. You can choose any space within your natural reach to place the creature in at the end of your drag (both of these count against the distance you can drag).Special: You must use at least one prehensile limb to initiate a drag on a creature, unless your weapon has the CM Drag property.
core-rules,-how-to-play/attacking/combat.sourcePath: Core Rules, How to Play/Attacking/Combat Maneuvers/Drag.md

core-rules,-how-to-play/attacking/combat.title: Shove
core-rules,-how-to-play/attacking/combat.description: Push the target 10ft away from you.
core-rules,-how-to-play/attacking/combat.sourcePath: Core Rules, How to Play/Attacking/Combat Maneuvers/Shove.md

core-rules,-how-to-play/attacking/crit.h.title: Crit
core-rules,-how-to-play/attacking/crit.h.description:
Critical hits occur when you roll 10 higher than a creature's AC. Crits deal 1.5x damage.Its also worth noting here that all damage multipliers are additive.
For example, group type enemies like swarms takes 1.5x damage from AoE. If you cleave and crit, you deal 2x damage.

core-rules,-how-to-play/attacking/damage.title: Damage
core-rules,-how-to-play/attacking/damage.description:
Damage is a value that subtracts from a target's +HP or Poise when the effect takes place.
Damage is always assigned a type. The physical damage types are Crush, Slash, and Pierce, and the elemental types are Force, Zap, Fire, Frost, Holy, Necrotic, Poison and Psychic. These are also tags. Poise damage is its own separate thing.If something deals multiple damage types, it usually adds both tags to the effect. For example, a flaming sword will deal Fire and Slash damage with its total damage.

core-rules,-how-to-play/attacking/dual-w.title: Dual Wielding
core-rules,-how-to-play/attacking/dual-w.description:
You can make attacks with weapons in both hands simultaneously as long as they both have the light property. Whenever you make an attack against a creature (unless +Combat Maneuver👐) with one of your weapons (the "main hand"), you can make an additional simple attack (that cannot be replaced with any other type of attack, including combat maneuvers) against the same creature with the other weapon (the "off hand") .Because you strike with the 2 weapons in tandem, if the "main hand" attack is enough to defeat a creature, you cannot make an "off hand" attack against a different creature.
If you make a special attack that involves making multiple attacks, such as the Cleave special attack, you can only make the "off hand" attack against the first creature you attack with it. If the special attack grants some special property to the weapon, like weapon toss allowing you to throw any weapon, it does not do so for the off-hand unless specified otherwise.If you gain additional limbs to wield weapons, you do not get more "main hand" or "off hand" attacks by default.You cannot dual wield with natural attacks or unarmed strikes by default.
core-rules,-how-to-play/attacking/dual-w.sourcePath: Core Rules, How to Play/Attacking/Dual Wielding.md

core-rules,-how-to-play/attacking/line-o.title: Line of Effect
core-rules,-how-to-play/attacking/line-o.description: A straight line between two places with no Total Cover or impassable obstacles for a given effect grants Line of Effect. This is different from sight, as you may be able to see someone and not Target them (such as through a window).
core-rules,-how-to-play/attacking/line-o.sourcePath: Core Rules, How to Play/Attacking/Line of Effect.md

core-rules,-how-to-play/death-and-resurr.title: Ashen One
core-rules,-how-to-play/death-and-resurr.description: In dark souls, certain types of creatures, namely the player character, hold a special place in the world's lore. When you die you don't reload the game, you canonically respawn at the location you last rested, leaving behind all your money where you died.You could choose to adopt a similar system where certain types of conditions need to be met for these unique creatures to die for real. Having the characters lose all their money might not be the best approach for a TTRPG: players like their money. But, in souls games you can go back to the place you died and collect the money again, so maybe.This kind of natural respawn mechanic is a good fit for campaigns where you expect your players to encounter dangerous creatures on the regular and your players don't get too discouraged from losing. Meat grinder without the consequences of losing your character for good. I will say though, dark souls is a very fast paced game where you can die every few minutes. In NN, many fights will likely last over an hour which makes the consequence of frequent death a bit more of a hassle.
core-rules,-how-to-play/death-and-resurr.sourcePath: Core Rules, How to Play/Death and Resurrection/Ashen One.md

core-rules,-how-to-play/death-and-resurr.title: Cloning Device
core-rules,-how-to-play/death-and-resurr.description: You start off your adventures waking up in some alchemist's lab, surrounded in copies of yourself. Whenever you die, there is a fresh body waiting for you back at the lab that your soul gets sucked into.This plays more into having a secret base type thing, and it feels a little less metagame-y than "chosen by god." it also has an interesting mystery component to it. Why were you guys chosen as clones? Whose lab is this? How's that for storytelling with resurrection?
core-rules,-how-to-play/death-and-resurr.sourcePath: Core Rules, How to Play/Death and Resurrection/Cloning Device.md

core-rules,-how-to-play/death-and-resurr.title: Limited Resurrection
core-rules,-how-to-play/death-and-resurr.description: Pose a caveat to resurrection magic that imposes a severely limiting factor, such as only being able to revive a creature shortly after it died with some kind of resource attached to it. Maybe even make it a limited resource by tying it to physical items, like scrolls with this effect attached to it.EFFECTYou breathe new life into a recently deceased creature. If the creature has died within the last minute, they are brought back to life at 1 hp and drained 10.
core-rules,-how-to-play/death-and-resurr.sourcePath: Core Rules, How to Play/Death and Resurrection/Limited Resurrection.md

core-rules,-how-to-play/death-and-resurr.title: Tombstone
core-rules,-how-to-play/death-and-resurr.description: In the event of your characters untimely demise, worry not, for the gods smile upon you. When killed, your body becomes a tombstone with your name and face on it. It weighs as much as you did, including all of your equipment. This tombstone can be carried back somewhere to perform a ritual and bring the character back to life.This can be a place of significance to this god, something generic like a church or something with more story relevance. It can be wherever home base is, or you can require the players to reach certain points in the campaign in order to get their characters resurrected (Ex: Your friend died by the lich's hand, and now, to get them back, you have to destroy his phylactery. Make a temp character!).The basic idea is there: satisfy this entity's conditions and life will be restored.
core-rules,-how-to-play/death-and-resurr.sourcePath: Core Rules, How to Play/Death and Resurrection/Tombstone.md

core-rules,-how-to-play/death-and-resurr.title: Withers
core-rules,-how-to-play/death-and-resurr.description: In Baldur's Gate 3, there is an NPC that shows up in your camp that has a vested interest in your success. He has powers that aren't like normal characters, chief among them the ability to resurrect fallen allies. You could easily introduce a similar character into your campaign, maybe even the introduction to the campaign is this NPC resurrecting the players.This particular method has the benefit of being less nebulous than divine forces. It gives someone the players can interact with and someone that can give them direction. Whatever the reason they have for resurrecting your players, it's because they need their help.
core-rules,-how-to-play/death-and-resurr.sourcePath: Core Rules, How to Play/Death and Resurrection/Withers.md

core-rules,-how-to-play/hitpoints/defeat.title: Defeat
core-rules,-how-to-play/hitpoints/defeat.description:
When you take damage that reduces you to zero hp, you are defeated, and must be healed to regain consciousness in a timely manner.
You can choose to non-lethally defeat someone provided you are using a Weapon Attack, unarmed strike or natural attack. If this is not the case, they must make a DC 8 luck check or die. Creatures that manage to survive being defeated have to keep making this luck check every time they take damage while defeated.
When a character recovers from the defeated condition, they are dazed on their next turn.
When recovering from the defeated condition, you also gain an Affliction.
When a main character🦸 (ie usually a player) falls to zero HP, they are not at risk of instant death. Instead of rolling luck checks, a main character gets a stack of Doom when they take damage while defeated. Upon acquiring the 5th stack, they die. Doom stacks are lost on rest.
See Recovering from Defeat for what happens when defeated creatures are left to their own devices.

core-rules,-how-to-play/hitpoints/healin.title: Healing
core-rules,-how-to-play/hitpoints/healin.description:
Healing is an effect that restores current +HP up to your maximum HP, grants Temp HP, or removes debilitating status conditions.
Healing effects do not work on Permanent Status, unless otherwise stated.

core-rules,-how-to-play/hitpoints/immuni.title: Immunity
core-rules,-how-to-play/hitpoints/immuni.description: A very rare defensive quality. You cannot be affected by a particular Damage type, tag or Status.

core-rules,-how-to-play/hitpoints/natura.title: Natural Healing
core-rules,-how-to-play/hitpoints/natura.description: In the absence of danger, a defeated creature will regain 1 hp after 1 hour. They are staggered until they are healed or they rest.With a proper 8 hours rest, a character restores all their HP, all of their daily use abilities and recover mana burn. You can only rest once each day.
core-rules,-how-to-play/hitpoints/natura.sourcePath: Core Rules, How to Play/Hitpoints/Natural Healing.md

core-rules,-how-to-play/hitpoints/recove.title: Recovering from Defeat
core-rules,-how-to-play/hitpoints/recove.description:
After being Defeated for an hour after the last time it took damage, a creature may attempt to shake off the condition with a STR Roll. On a 10 or higher, they lose the Defeated condition, but as long as their +HP remains 0, they are Staggered.
After successfully recovering, the creature is Drained 5.
core-rules,-how-to-play/hitpoints/recove.sourcePath: Core Rules, How to Play/Hitpoints/Recovering from Defeat.md

core-rules,-how-to-play/hitpoints/resist.title: Resistance
core-rules,-how-to-play/hitpoints/resist.description:
Having resistance to a Damage type makes you take half damage from it.
Having resistance to a Status effect gives you a +4 bonus to saves against effects with that tag.

core-rules,-how-to-play/hitpoints/rest.h.title: Rest
core-rules,-how-to-play/hitpoints/rest.h.description:
Eight consecutive hours of sleep. If you sleep in undesirable conditions, or if your rest is interrupted, you do not gain the benefits of rest, and you are exhausted the following day. You can sleep in an extra two hours to negate any interruptions.
In order to rest, you must be in some type of sanctuary. A sanctuary is typically something where you and your friends are not the only allies around. It must be comfortable and reasonably quiet. It also does not have enemies lurking just around the corner. Typical sanctuaries include civilization, a camp site nestled in a cave or a region well-defended by allies, such as those protected by a great fairy.
When you rest, you restore your HP and Mana Burn. You recover 1 stack of drain. You also can use abilities with limited uses per day, such as recharge abilities.

core-rules,-how-to-play/hitpoints/temp-h.title: Temp HP
core-rules,-how-to-play/hitpoints/temp-h.description: Temporary Hitpoints (Temp HP) are gained separately from your +HP. They are lost before your HP, and multiple sources do not stack - only the highest applies.Unless otherwise stated, Temp HP only lasts 1 minute.
core-rules,-how-to-play/hitpoints/temp-h.sourcePath: Core Rules, How to Play/Hitpoints/Temp HP.md

core-rules,-how-to-play/hitpoints/weakne.title: Weakness
core-rules,-how-to-play/hitpoints/weakne.description:
Having weakness means you take more damage from a specifc Damage type. It is expressed in numerical values like "Holy 3." Denoting that if an attack does holy damage, after all damage calculation, it deals 3 more.
Creatures can also have a weakness to something that isnt damage. They have a -4 penalty to Saves against effects of a certain Tag.

core-rules,-how-to-play/more-rules/fall-.title: Fall Damage
core-rules,-how-to-play/more-rules/fall-.description:
Fall damage increases by 3 Crush for every 10 feet you fall, capped at 60 damage. Every 50 feet you are also Drained 5, capped at 20. You take Poise damage equal to the crush damage you took. If this breaks your poise, you are Knocked Down.
When determining fall distance, subtract your Enhanced Jump.
core-rules,-how-to-play/more-rules/fall-.sourcePath: Core Rules, How to Play/More Rules/Fall Damage.md

core-rules,-how-to-play/more-rules/light.title: Light Level
core-rules,-how-to-play/more-rules/light.description:
Light levels have 3 distinct categories.Bright Light - A sunny day or a torch lit room. Bright light let's creatures see things clearly. Most creatures can see in bright light without any penalty. Sources of bright light taper off into dim light before turning into darkness. For instance a Torch gives 20 ft of bright light, so it would give an equal amount of distance of dim light.
Dim Light - Moonlight or at the edge of your torch light. Many humanoids cannot see well in dim light. Features in dim light appear only as a silhouette with dull, if any, color. Without special senses, creatures have Partial Concealment in dim light.
Darkness - The depths of a cave or deep underwater. Few creatures can see clearly in a complete darkness. Some, such as Humans, can't see at all. Those that can (such as with Nightvision or Darkvision) still only see in grayscale. Without special senses, creatures have Total Concealment in darkness.
core-rules,-how-to-play/more-rules/light.sourcePath: Core Rules, How to Play/More Rules/Light Level.md

core-rules,-how-to-play/more-rules/round.title: Rounding Numbers
core-rules,-how-to-play/more-rules/round.sourcePath: Core Rules, How to Play/More Rules/Rounding Numbers.md

core-rules,-how-to-play/more-rules/stack.title: Stacking Damage and Defense
core-rules,-how-to-play/more-rules/stack.description:
When you stack DR and Resistance, add them together in the way that reduces damage the most.When you have multiple sources of increasing damage by a percentage, add the percentages together, do not multiply (ie 1.5x dmg and 1.5x dmg adds together to 2x dmg).
This can happen in rare circumstances where you Crit a swarm with cleave for instance.
When you have multiple sources of halving damage, such as through a passed Save and Resistance, then you take 50% of the halved damage (20 damage fireblast halved to 10, then halved again to 5).
When you have Resistance against an effect that has a multiplier to damage, such as a Crit, apply the resistance to the final damage of the crit (10 damage gunshot, 15 crit, 7 with resistance).
core-rules,-how-to-play/more-rules/stack.sourcePath: Core Rules, How to Play/More Rules/Stacking Damage and Defense.md

core-rules,-how-to-play/saving-throws/fo.title: Fortitude
core-rules,-how-to-play/saving-throws/fo.description:
Fortitude Saves are one of the three primary Saves Rolled to avoid a negative effect.
Your Fortitude represents your resistance to physical hardship, such as Venom and concussive attacks.
You add STR and LvL to your Fortitude, as well as any bonuses from your +Class.
core-rules,-how-to-play/saving-throws/fo.sourcePath: Core Rules, How to Play/Saving Throws/Fortitude.md

core-rules,-how-to-play/saving-throws/re.title: Reflex
core-rules,-how-to-play/saving-throws/re.description:
Reflex Saves are one of the three primary Saves Rolled to avoid a negative effect.
Your Reflex represents your reactions and ability to evade or mitigate sudden attacks such as AoE.
You add DEX and LvL to your Reflex, as well as any bonuses from your +Class.
core-rules,-how-to-play/saving-throws/re.sourcePath: Core Rules, How to Play/Saving Throws/Reflex.md

core-rules,-how-to-play/saving-throws/wi.title: Will
core-rules,-how-to-play/saving-throws/wi.description:
Will Saves are one of the three primary Saves Rolled to avoid a negative effect.
Your Will represents your mental resilience and ability to resist mental attacks such as Illusions, mind control, and Fear.
You add WIS and LvL to your Will, as well as any bonuses from your +Class.
core-rules,-how-to-play/saving-throws/wi.sourcePath: Core Rules, How to Play/Saving Throws/Will.md

core-rules,-how-to-play/status-effects/a.title: Ablaze
core-rules,-how-to-play/status-effects/a.description: When a creature is set Ablaze, it takes 2d8 Fire Damage at the start of each turn. Attacking creatures get a +2 bonus to Attack. On every turn after the first, it gets a Reflex save before it takes damage to end the effect. A creature can choose to inflict Knockdown on itself at the end of its turn for a +4 bonus to this save.Being submerged in water, getting entombed or taking cold damage also removes this condition. Other things that snuff out flames can reasonably remove ablaze.
core-rules,-how-to-play/status-effects/a.sourcePath: Core Rules, How to Play/Status Effects/Ablaze.md

core-rules,-how-to-play/status-effects/a.title: Affliction
core-rules,-how-to-play/status-effects/a.description:
A type of permanent negative effect that can usually only be removed by taking some time off to rest, recuperate and relax. Afflictions come in tiers from 1-3. Higher tier afflictions usually require more extreme forms of care to remove. They are Permanent Status.
See Afflictions for more details.
core-rules,-how-to-play/status-effects/a.sourcePath: Core Rules, How to Play/Status Effects/Affliction.md

core-rules,-how-to-play/status-effects/a.title: Anchored
core-rules,-how-to-play/status-effects/a.description: Creature cannot use Teleportation effects. Either on themselves or on others. If they attempt to do so, the effect fizzles.
core-rules,-how-to-play/status-effects/a.sourcePath: Core Rules, How to Play/Status Effects/Anchored.md

core-rules,-how-to-play/status-effects/a.title: Asleep
core-rules,-how-to-play/status-effects/a.description:
Creature loses Concentration.
This creature is Knocked Down, can take no actions, and cannot be awakened unless it takes damage, is subject to an offensive ability or an ally uses the Aid action to awaken them. The creature is also DD and suffers -10 +Perception👀.If the creature is asleep through natural means, it can use perception to wake up by noticing something amiss.
core-rules,-how-to-play/status-effects/a.sourcePath: Core Rules, How to Play/Status Effects/Asleep.md

core-rules,-how-to-play/status-effects/b.title: Bleeding
core-rules,-how-to-play/status-effects/b.description:
Bleeding creatures take a specified amount of True Damage at the start of each of their turns for a specified duration. If no duration is specified, it lasts indefinitely. The DC to stop the bleeding (with the +Medicine💉 skill, or magic healing with a CL check) is the attacker's LvL+12.
Instead of taking damage, bleed prevents a creature from losing the Defeated condition when healed (unless the healing removes the bleed).Bleed effects do not stack. Only use the most severe effect.
core-rules,-how-to-play/status-effects/b.sourcePath: Core Rules, How to Play/Status Effects/Bleeding.md

core-rules,-how-to-play/status-effects/b.title: Blinded
core-rules,-how-to-play/status-effects/b.description: Sighted creature takes a -10 penalty to +Perception👀 and treats all creatures as though they had Total Concealment. Creatures' vision range decreases to 10 ft. Creature is also DD.
core-rules,-how-to-play/status-effects/b.sourcePath: Core Rules, How to Play/Status Effects/Blinded.md

core-rules,-how-to-play/status-effects/b.title: Blurred Vision
core-rules,-how-to-play/status-effects/b.description: Sighted creature takes a -4 penalty to +Perception👀 and treats all creatures as though they had Partial Concealment.
core-rules,-how-to-play/status-effects/b.sourcePath: Core Rules, How to Play/Status Effects/Blurred Vision.md

core-rules,-how-to-play/status-effects/c.title: Charmed
core-rules,-how-to-play/status-effects/c.description:
Creature cannot attack the entity that inflicted this condition. The entity that inflicted this condition has a +4 bonus on Charisma Skills against this creature.This ends if the creature that inflicted the condition harms the charmed creature.Charmed creatures always interpret what the creature that charmed them is doing in the most positive light: Punches and sword swings are massages and surgeries. Charmed creatures are often willing to do things asked of them provided they don't put the creature in danger or clash with their ethos. After the charm ends, acts are seen for what they truly are.
Charmed can be removed by an ally that realizes something is up by taking the Aid action.
core-rules,-how-to-play/status-effects/c.sourcePath: Core Rules, How to Play/Status Effects/Charmed.md

core-rules,-how-to-play/status-effects/c.title: Clumsy
core-rules,-how-to-play/status-effects/c.description: Creature takes a stacking penalty to Reflex and AC equal to the Clumsy value. This otherwise functions like Shaken. A Clumsy creature cannot ascend using Flight, or things that function similarly to flight, such as a Hover Speed.
core-rules,-how-to-play/status-effects/c.sourcePath: Core Rules, How to Play/Status Effects/Clumsy.md

core-rules,-how-to-play/status-effects/c.title: Confused
core-rules,-how-to-play/status-effects/c.description: You consider all creatures enemies. Every turn, roll a d10 to determine how you act. Many effects allow you to increase the dice roll with a will save. For confusion effects that last more than 1 round, each subsequent d10 roll gets 2 added to the result.The confusion result is the only thing the creature does on their turn, ie if you roll a 5 you wander and then end turn.
core-rules,-how-to-play/status-effects/c.sourcePath: Core Rules, How to Play/Status Effects/Confused.md

core-rules,-how-to-play/status-effects/c.title: Cursed
core-rules,-how-to-play/status-effects/c.description: A Cursed creature is suffering from a permanent debilitating condition. Curses cannot be dispelled, but they all have some way to get rid of them. This usually requires some convoluted action most people wouldn't do unless prompted. Can be identified using the "identify curse or affliction" feature in the +Medicine💉 skill.
core-rules,-how-to-play/status-effects/c.sourcePath: Core Rules, How to Play/Status Effects/Cursed.md

core-rules,-how-to-play/status-effects/d.title: Dazed
core-rules,-how-to-play/status-effects/d.description:
Creature loses Concentration.
A more severe version of Staggered. Creature cannot take a Standard Action and cannot make AoOs.
core-rules,-how-to-play/status-effects/d.sourcePath: Core Rules, How to Play/Status Effects/Dazed.md

core-rules,-how-to-play/status-effects/d.title: Defeated
core-rules,-how-to-play/status-effects/d.description:
A defeated creature is Knocked Down and cannot do anything more than a weakly speak while at or below 0 HP. Main characters🦸 may crawl at a rate of 10 feet per turn, or move at full speed when another creature uses Aid.
When recovering from the defeated condition, a creature immediately loses the knocked down condition and instead becomes Dazed for 1 round.
See Defeat for more details.
core-rules,-how-to-play/status-effects/d.sourcePath: Core Rules, How to Play/Status Effects/Defeated.md

core-rules,-how-to-play/status-effects/d.title: Dominated
core-rules,-how-to-play/status-effects/d.description: A creature that is dominated is hit with a powerful charm effect, possessed, or controlled by some other means. They are unable to control their own actions and are subject to the will of another creature.
core-rules,-how-to-play/status-effects/d.sourcePath: Core Rules, How to Play/Status Effects/Dominated.md

core-rules,-how-to-play/status-effects/d.title: Drained
core-rules,-how-to-play/status-effects/d.description:
Lowers your current and maximum +HP by 1 for each stack. One point is removed with a day of Rest (or more quickly with +Medicine💉).A creature with enough drain to decrease their max hp to 0 dies.
Some circumstances, such as when a healing effect also inflicts drain for a powerful effect, you can reasonably ignore the current HP reduction.
core-rules,-how-to-play/status-effects/d.sourcePath: Core Rules, How to Play/Status Effects/Drained.md

core-rules,-how-to-play/status-effects/e.title: Entangled
core-rules,-how-to-play/status-effects/e.description: Creature gets -2 AC, and their Land Speed is reduced to zero. This condition usually comes with a means to escape manually with +Athletics🏊. Creatures without the entangled condition receive a +5 bonus on checks to untangle a creature.
core-rules,-how-to-play/status-effects/e.sourcePath: Core Rules, How to Play/Status Effects/Entangled.md

core-rules,-how-to-play/status-effects/e.title: Entombed
core-rules,-how-to-play/status-effects/e.description: The creature is encased in ice, stone etc. They have Total Cover and are Untargetable. Entombed creatures can only perform mental actions or try to escape (usually requiring an athletics check).
core-rules,-how-to-play/status-effects/e.sourcePath: Core Rules, How to Play/Status Effects/Entombed.md

core-rules,-how-to-play/status-effects/f.title: Fascinated
core-rules,-how-to-play/status-effects/f.description: Creature cannot take actions other than watch the source of its fascination. Creature loses this condition after it is attacked, has a +Saving Throw inflicted on it, or succeeds on a +Perception👀 check to notice a creature in its pockets or otherwise taking an offensive action. If the source of its fascination is no longer visible (or able to be sensed for other types of fascination), the condition also ends. After this happens, the creature temporarily becomes immune to fascination for 1 minute.
core-rules,-how-to-play/status-effects/f.sourcePath: Core Rules, How to Play/Status Effects/Fascinated.md

core-rules,-how-to-play/status-effects/f.title: Fatigued
core-rules,-how-to-play/status-effects/f.description:
Cannot Charge or Dash.
Jump distance is halved (minimum 5). This is applies after all other jump modifiers (like Enhanced Jump)
-4 +Athletics🏊, +Perception👀 and +Acrobatics⚖. Removed after 10 minutes of inactivity.
Doing anything that causes you to become fatigued again while already fatigued instead causes you to become Exhausted
core-rules,-how-to-play/status-effects/f.sourcePath: Core Rules, How to Play/Status Effects/Fatigued.md

core-rules,-how-to-play/status-effects/f.title: Frightened
core-rules,-how-to-play/status-effects/f.description: Creature cannot move closer to the source of its fear. It has disadvantage on attacks and opposed skill checks against the source of its fear.
core-rules,-how-to-play/status-effects/f.sourcePath: Core Rules, How to Play/Status Effects/Frightened.md

core-rules,-how-to-play/status-effects/g.title: Glowing
core-rules,-how-to-play/status-effects/g.description:
Creature emits Bright Light with a 5 ft radius, causing it to suffer -10 +Stealth. Creatures attacking a glowing creature get a +2 bonus to Attack.
The acc boost does not stack with Ablaze.
core-rules,-how-to-play/status-effects/g.sourcePath: Core Rules, How to Play/Status Effects/Glowing.md

core-rules,-how-to-play/status-effects/g.title: Grounded
core-rules,-how-to-play/status-effects/g.description: Through bent wings, malfunctioning magic, or disorientation, the creature is unable to stay airborne. Creatures currently flying immediately plummet and provoke AoOs, but retain enough flight to avoid Fall Damage. This also affects Hover speeds.
core-rules,-how-to-play/status-effects/g.sourcePath: Core Rules, How to Play/Status Effects/Grounded.md

core-rules,-how-to-play/status-effects/h.title: Held Down
core-rules,-how-to-play/status-effects/h.description:
Creature cannot stand up and is persistently Knocked Down
A creature who is grappled is automatically also Held Down
core-rules,-how-to-play/status-effects/h.sourcePath: Core Rules, How to Play/Status Effects/Held Down.md

core-rules,-how-to-play/status-effects/i.title: Invincible
core-rules,-how-to-play/status-effects/i.description: Creature's +HP cannot be reduced.
core-rules,-how-to-play/status-effects/i.sourcePath: Core Rules, How to Play/Status Effects/Invincible.md

core-rules,-how-to-play/status-effects/i.title: Invisible
core-rules,-how-to-play/status-effects/i.description: You cannot be detected by sight. This grants you Total Concealment against any creature that primarily uses sight. You must still use +Stealth to hide your presence and specific location, or else creatures will still be able to attack your space to try and hit you.
core-rules,-how-to-play/status-effects/i.sourcePath: Core Rules, How to Play/Status Effects/Invisible.md

core-rules,-how-to-play/status-effects/k.title: Knocked Down
core-rules,-how-to-play/status-effects/k.description: Creature takes a -30 penalty to speed and attacks get a +2 bonus to attack against them until the start of the inflicting creature's next turn, at which point the condition ends, unless the creature is Held Down.
core-rules,-how-to-play/status-effects/k.sourcePath: Core Rules, How to Play/Status Effects/Knocked Down.md

core-rules,-how-to-play/status-effects/m.title: Mindless
core-rules,-how-to-play/status-effects/m.description:
Creature does not have any capacity for reasoning. It performs basic motions regardless of external stimuli. Mindless creatures do not possess an INT score.
This status grants Immunity to Mind-Affecting effects.
core-rules,-how-to-play/status-effects/m.sourcePath: Core Rules, How to Play/Status Effects/Mindless.md

core-rules,-how-to-play/status-effects/p.title: Pacified
core-rules,-how-to-play/status-effects/p.description: The creature cannot take aggressive actions against enemies with intent to inflict damage or Status or assist its allies in inflicting damage.
core-rules,-how-to-play/status-effects/p.sourcePath: Core Rules, How to Play/Status Effects/Pacified.md

core-rules,-how-to-play/status-effects/s.title: Shaken
core-rules,-how-to-play/status-effects/s.description: Creature takes a penalty to Will and Potency equal to the Shaken value. Adding new stacks of Shaken gives all stacks the longest duration of all the effects.Usually, Shaken wears off after 1 minute out of combat.
core-rules,-how-to-play/status-effects/s.sourcePath: Core Rules, How to Play/Status Effects/Shaken.md

core-rules,-how-to-play/status-effects/s.title: Sickened
core-rules,-how-to-play/status-effects/s.description: Creature takes a penalty to Fortitude and Attack equal to the Sickened value. Otherwise functions like Shaken. Sickened usually wears off after 1 minute out of combat.
core-rules,-how-to-play/status-effects/s.sourcePath: Core Rules, How to Play/Status Effects/Sickened.md

core-rules,-how-to-play/status-effects/s.title: Silenced
core-rules,-how-to-play/status-effects/s.description: Creature cannot speak, including to cast spells or communicate information via +Monster Lore📖.Spells that state an absence of speech can still be cast.
core-rules,-how-to-play/status-effects/s.sourcePath: Core Rules, How to Play/Status Effects/Silenced.md

core-rules,-how-to-play/status-effects/s.title: Siphoned
core-rules,-how-to-play/status-effects/s.description: The creature is severed from its magic. It is not capable of casting Spells, Concentration, or using its activating Su abilities. Constant effects, effects from items, or effects that were already cast remain in effect.
core-rules,-how-to-play/status-effects/s.sourcePath: Core Rules, How to Play/Status Effects/Siphoned.md

core-rules,-how-to-play/status-effects/s.title: Staggered
core-rules,-how-to-play/status-effects/s.description: Creature can only take a Standard Action or Swift Action each turn, not both. -15 Land Speed.
core-rules,-how-to-play/status-effects/s.sourcePath: Core Rules, How to Play/Status Effects/Staggered.md

core-rules,-how-to-play/status-effects/s.title: Stasis
core-rules,-how-to-play/status-effects/s.description: Creature is frozen in time, or some other particularly powerful effect. They are Untargetable, Unassailable, Unstoppable and Invincible. They cannot take any actions unless otherwise stated.
core-rules,-how-to-play/status-effects/s.sourcePath: Core Rules, How to Play/Status Effects/Stasis.md

core-rules,-how-to-play/status-effects/s.title: Status
core-rules,-how-to-play/status-effects/s.description: A status effect is a condition that is placed on a creature to apply CC, change their rolls, and otherwise modify how they interact with the world... For better or for worse.
core-rules,-how-to-play/status-effects/s.sourcePath: Core Rules, How to Play/Status Effects/Status.md

core-rules,-how-to-play/status-effects/s.title: Stunned
core-rules,-how-to-play/status-effects/s.description:
Creature loses Concentration.
A more extreme form of being Dazed. Creature cannot take any actions or movement. Creature is DD.
core-rules,-how-to-play/status-effects/s.sourcePath: Core Rules, How to Play/Status Effects/Stunned.md

core-rules,-how-to-play/status-effects/s.title: Submerged
core-rules,-how-to-play/status-effects/s.description: Target is completely surrounded in liquid. This triggers Aquatic Combat and Improved Cover.
core-rules,-how-to-play/status-effects/s.sourcePath: Core Rules, How to Play/Status Effects/Submerged.md

core-rules,-how-to-play/status-effects/t.title: Taunted
